title.narrative: Catalyzing the Nature-Positive Transformation of the Agricultural Sector in Turkmenistan towards Enhanced Resilience to Climate Change project

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment [48] 147. The project will deliver significant socioeconomic benefits at both national and local levels by enhancing agricultural productivity, building resilience to climate change, and fostering sustainable livelihoods. At the local level, the project will directly benefit farming communities by introducing nature-positive and climate-resilient practices that improve soil health, reduce water wastage, and increase crop yields. These interventions will diversify income streams through agroforestry, salinity-tolerant crops, and improved irrigation systems. Training programs and capacity-building initiatives will empower farmers, including women and marginalized groups, equipping them with knowledge and tools to adopt sustainable practices, while demonstration plots will serve as practical models for innovation. 148. At the national level, the project will contribute to food security and economic stability by reducing the vulnerability of agricultural systems to climate impacts. By aligning with national development strategies, the project will strengthen institutional capacities and foster the adoption of policies that promote sustainable agriculture, reduce GHG emissions, and combat land degradation. The socioeconomic benefits also directly support global environmental benefits (GEBs) by restoring degraded lands, conserving biodiversity, and enhancing carbon sinks through improved land and water management. These outcomes reduce GHG emissions, increase ecosystem resilience, and contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). 149. Furthermore, the project will actively promote decent work and productive employment in rural areas, aligning with international labor principles. Through capacity-building activities, training programs, and the dissemination of best practices, the project will empower local communities to engage in sustainable agriculture and natural resource management practices, enhancing their livelihoods and overall well-being. By fostering inclusive and participatory approaches, the project will ensure equitable distribution of the benefits derived from sustainable resource management, promoting social cohesion and economic development in Lebap region of Turkmenistan. [48] Specific guidance on how FAO can promote the Four Pillars of Decent Work in rural areas is provided in the Quick reference for addressing decent rural employment (as well as in the full corresponding Guidance document). For more information on FAO’s work on decent rural employment and related guidance materials please consult the FAO thematic website at: http://www.fao.org/rural-employment/en/.

To enable a transformative shift towards nature-positive, resilient and sustainable management of natural resources, especially the holistic integration of NBS practices at the different connected landscapes, in order to improve biodiversity conservation and environmental sustainability of food systems in Turkmenistan
